newsitem.title: SPAIN: Euro to cut Spain bank revenues 15 pct - Argentaria.
newsitem.headline: Euro to cut Spain bank revenues 15 pct - Argentaria.

text.p: Argentaria Managing Director Francisco Gomez Roldan said on Thursday the euro could cut Spanish bank revenues by at least 15 percent with wholesale banking, Treasury and foreign business hard hit.

"There are estimates that see a decline of 15 percent to 18 percent from current levels in those areas, which entities could lose directly as a consequence of EMU," according to the summary of a speech Gomez Roldan gave in Santander.
He estimated the Spanish banking industry would spend some 100 billion pesetas preparing for the euro, primarily in information technology.

"The ultimate consequence of these impacts, with higher costs and the loss of revenue, will be a deterioration of the levels of efficiency of the institutions short-term," according to the summary made available in Madrid.
He added that Spanish banks would face fierce competition in two different areas.

"On the one hand, companies with a strong retail distribution network may decide to enter into product and financial services distribution, and on the other hand, specialists in concrete business segments, such as consumer credit, credit cards or investment funds and other specialised players could be competition of the first degree," he said.
